summary.short: Reconciliation statute (Pub. L. 119-21, dated July 4, 2025) with mainly fiscal provisions across tax, nutrition, agriculture, health, education, immigration fees, energy leasing, transportation and defense; includes appropriations for defense AI programs.
summary.long: Public Law 119-21, an Act to provide for reconciliation pursuant to title II of H. Con. Res. 14, dated July 4, 2025, is a fiscal statute organized by House committee title. It appropriates or rescinds funds, and extends, modifies or terminates programs and tax provisions. Title I (agriculture) amends the Food and Nutrition Act and the Agricultural Act of 2014 and sets crop insurance and conservation funding. Title II appropriates defense funds. Title III changes the CFPB funding cap and the SEC reserve fund. Title IV covers the Coast Guard, spectrum auctions, air traffic control, space launch fees, NASA, fuel economy penalties and airport lease payments. Title V repeals energy provisions of the Inflation Reduction Act and sets oil, gas and coal leasing duties. Title VI rescinds environmental funds. Title VII covers tax rates, credits and deductions, terminates clean energy credits, and sets Medicaid, ACA premium credit and Medicare eligibility rules. Title VIII covers student loans and Pell grants; Title IX covers border security and homeland funding; Title X covers immigration fees and appropriations. AI-related provisions are defense and government appropriations.

notes: This part covers the table of contents and Titles I to V (Sec. 10101 to 50103); Titles VI onward are in other parts, although the table of contents lists them. Most sections here are appropriations, rescissions or program funding levels; the enumerated amounts are not coded as thresholds in this part. Several sections rescind unobligated balances of appropriations made by Public Law 117-169 (e.g., Sec. 10201, 10601(g), 30002, 40008, 40010) and Sec. 40011 rescinds CHIPS Act balances. Sec. 40005 refers to the Administration and its Administrator without expanding the term in this part. No internal inconsistency was identified in this part. Part 2 of 5 covers Sec. 50104 to Sec. 70342. Several cross-referenced provisions (e.g., Public Law 115-97 section 20001, Mineral Leasing Act section 35) are not reproduced in this part. Many Title VII provisions amend the Internal Revenue Code and are coded as one relation row. Rescissions of unobligated balances (e.g., Sec. 50304, Sec. 50402(b), Secs. 60001-60024) do not repeal the underlying sections unless the text says so. Sec. 50404 (transformational AI models) is AI-relevant and appropriates $150,000,000 through September 30, 2026. Section status fields below are set to not_applicable only because the schema requires a value; relations and entities are coded above. Covers SEC. 70354 to SEC. 70524 of the Act. Relations and entities cover this part only. The many Internal Revenue Code amendments are one relation row because the Code is not a registry instrument. Heading of SEC. 70432 says repeal of a revision, but the text reinstates an earlier exception. Wind and solar termination rules differ: SEC. 70512(a) keys to placed-in-service dates, SEC. 70513(a) to placed-in-service dates for qualified property, and SEC. 70512(l)(4) and 70513(g)(5) to construction start 12 months after enactment. Regulatory material (Internal Revenue Service Notice 2025-08, Treasury Regulation section 1.45X-4(c)(4)(i), 90 Fed. Reg. 22711) is cited but not coded. Part 4 covers SEC. 70525 to SEC. 83001(b). Amendments to external statutes (Internal Revenue Code, Social Security Act, Higher Education Act, Tariff Act, PPACA) are coded as relations with an empty target_instrument_id because targets are not in the registry. The HEA repeal of section 455(e) (Sec. 82001(c)(1)) falls under the HEA amends row. CMS rules named in Sec. 71101, 71102 and 71111 (88 Fed. Reg. 65230; 89 Fed. Reg. 22780; 89 Fed. Reg. 40876) are subject to implementation moratoria through 30 September 2034, not repeal, and are not coded as relations. Sec. 71103 and 71104 both amend SSA 1902(a); 71104 applies to paragraph (88) as amended by 71103. The Tariff Act section 321 penalty takes effect 30 days after enactment (Sec. 70531(a)(2)) while the repeal of the commercial shipment exception takes effect 1 July 2027 (Sec. 70531(b)(3)); these are separate amendments, not conflicting dates. Part 5 of 5 covers Sec. 83002 through Sec. 100205 only; other parts are annotated separately. Target instrument IDs are empty because no registry IDs were supplied. Sec. 85001-85002 state that the 2022 regulations 'shall not be in effect' for loans first originating before July 1, 2035 and restore earlier rules; the text does not repeal them. Sec. 100015 inserts INA 286(w), which refers to 'section 100015 of the Act' (this instrument). Fee sections let the Secretary or Attorney General set amounts by rule above stated minimums; the fixed amounts are as stated in the text.
